sentences.text: Dipturus is a large genus of fish belonging to the class Chondrichthyes, the order Rajiformes, and the family Rajidae.
Scientists currently recognize 39 distinct species within this group.
The genus was first described by Rafinesque in 1810.
The type species of the genus Dipturus is Raja batis.
Species in the genus Dipturus were formerly classified within the genus Raja, though some were later moved to Dentiraja, Spiniraja, and Zearaja.
Modern species live in temperate and subtropical waters across the Atlantic, western Indian, eastern Pacific, and Mediterranean Seas.
Fossil records show the genus existed from the Rupelian to the Tortonian, spanning 33.9 to 7.246 million years ago.
